claims.text: The initial catalyst consists of Pt nanoparticles dispersed on a ceria-zirconia support.
A sub-nanometer, conformal alumina coating can be deposited on the Pt/ceria-zirconia catalyst by atomic layer deposition.
The ALD alumina layer creates anchoring sites for Pt.
The alumina modification promotes atomically dispersed Pt or very small Pt clusters at the alumina/ceria-zirconia interface.
The ALD-deposited alumina increases interfacial interactions between Pt and the support.
Stronger Pt-support interactions hinder Pt sintering and agglomeration during high-temperature redox cycling.
Suppressing Pt sintering improves catalytic activity.
Suppressing Pt sintering prolongs catalyst durability.
The ALD-modified catalyst can retain improved activity and durability at a lower Pt loading than the unmodified catalyst.
The ALD-modified catalyst will increase conversion efficiency by approximately 10% relative to the unmodified Pt/ceria-zirconia baseline.
The ALD-modified catalyst will deactivate more slowly than the unmodified baseline over extended cycling.
The predicted benefits will hold during high-temperature exposure at 800–1000°C with redox cycling and relevant automotive exhaust gas compositions.
The benefits may be less pronounced at substantially lower temperatures or under static operating conditions.
